0.long_answer: Removal of the medial temporal lobe, which includes critical structures like the hippocampus, primarily disrupts the brain's ability to consolidate new information into long-term memory. This leads to an inability to form new memories, a condition known as anterograde amnesia. Although there can sometimes be a degree of retrograde amnesia (loss of memories formed prior to the surgery), the hallmark and most significant effect of medial temporal lobe removal is the development of anterograde amnesia.
